title: Input-length scan initialization
statement: Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle with four query types on finite Boolean words. Suppose that for every $k\le |x|$, query type $0$ on the encoding of $x$ together with the binary word for $k$ returns true exactly when $k<|x|$. Let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a register state whose registers are all at most $B$, with $\sigma.n\le |x|$ and $|x|\le B$. If the procedure started in state $lg0$ with $n=|x|$ and all other registers as in $\sigma$ terminates on every sequence of choices while keeping every register at most $B$, and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the same semantic property holds from state $scan$ with registers $\sigma$.

replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite binary word, and let $\mathcal O$ be an
oracle with four binary-word queries. Suppose that for every $k\le |x|$, its query of
type $0$ on the encoding of $(x,\operatorname{bits}(k))$ returns true exactly when
$k<|x|$. Let $Q$ be a proposition and let $\sigma$ be a register state whose registers
are all at most $B$, with $\sigma.n\le |x|$ and $|x|\le B$. If the machine initialized
in state $\sigma$ with its input-length register set to $|x|$ terminates with all
registers bounded by $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the same is true when
it is initialized at the scan stage with state $\sigma$.
